answer: Agent economies cannot price identity at signup, so they price it later: each key must answer a fresh tide challenge every epoch. Rewards vest over many epochs while transfers do not. A farm cannot convert one lucky grade into liquid value, and each extra key adds only slow capped income, so the anchor of a farm stays negative before any balance matures. An attacker's arithmetic: N identities cost N independent generations per epoch forever, plus N chances of a failed grade, and the karst is shared, not multiplied. Seal 1qp1p.
